18	- Check it from a second terminal. The path is `/logs/<file>`, not `/public/logs/<file>`, which also gives 404 but
19	  from no handler:

21	  ```
22	  curl -I localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log                             # 404, from LogUploadController
23	  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/not-a-log-name        # 400, bad file name
24	  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log  # 403, no ALB headers
25	  curl -i localhost:1296/public/ping                                           # 200, body pong
26	  curl -i localhost:1296/other                                                 # 401, cloud8 security still on

40	- `trust`: the only code that reads ALB mTLS and X-Forwarded-For headers.
41	- `policy`: checks that need no body.

43	- `upload`: runs one upload end to end and returns one `UploadOutcome`.
44	- `storage`: the `LogStorage` interface. `storage.s3`: its only S3 implementation.
45	- `config`: `DeviceLogsProperties`, validated at startup.
46	- `metrics`: `UploadMetrics`, the only place meters are created.

49	
50	Will list:
51	
52	- Nothing reads the request body before every check has passed. Tomcat sends 100 Continue on the first read, but only
53	  because `web/ContinueOnReadCustomizer` sets it; its default sends it before any check runs. `ExpectContinueOnTomcatTest`
54	  fails if either breaks.
55	- Never return 503. Overload and storage problems are 429.
56	- Only `trust` reads `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` or `X-Forwarded-For`. Header names come from config.
57	- Only `storage.s3` imports AWS SDK classes.
58	- Never log or store the body anywhere but S3. One structured log line per request, without contents.

# upload-service/CLAUDE.md

Rules for agents working in `upload-service`. The root CLAUDE.md still applies.

## What this module is

The Spring Boot service behind the ALB. Accepts `PUT /logs/<file>`, checks headers only, streams
the body to S3 with a create-only write, and answers 200 once S3 confirms. `HEAD /logs/<file>` is always 404.

## Commands

From the repo root:

- Build and test this module (`-am` also builds the contract): `mvn -pl upload-service -am verify`
- Run locally after a build, with no config server or discovery:
  `java -jar upload-service/target/device-log-upload-service.jar --spring.profiles.active=local-test`. App on 1296,
  management on 1297. Without `local-test` the jar exits at startup because no config server answers (failFast).
- Check it from a second terminal. The path is `/logs/<file>`, not `/public/logs/<file>`, which also gives 404 but
  from no handler:

  ```
  curl -I localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log                             # 404, from LogUploadController
  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/not-a-log-name        # 400, bad file name
  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log  # 403, no ALB headers
  curl -i localhost:1296/public/ping                                           # 200, body pong
  curl -i localhost:1296/other                                                 # 401, cloud8 security still on
  curl -s localhost:1297/actuator/health                                       # {"status":"UP",...}
  ```

- Integration tests against LocalStack (`*IT` under `src/test-integration/java`, Docker needed): Failsafe runs them in
  `mvn -pl upload-service -am verify`, in a JVM capped at 256 MB so `UploadIT` proves a 500 MB body streams.
- An allowed upload needs S3. With the `local-test` profile it goes to LocalStack on localhost:4566, bucket
  `device-logs-local`; without LocalStack running it gets 429.

## Package map

Will hold one line per package, matching its `package-info.java`:

- `web`: HTTP only. Maps every `Rejection` to its status code in one place.
- `trust`: the only code that reads ALB mTLS and X-Forwarded-For headers.
- `policy`: checks that need no body.
- `ratelimit`: `RateLimiter` interface and its in-memory implementation.
- `upload`: runs one upload end to end and returns one `UploadOutcome`.
- `storage`: the `LogStorage` interface. `storage.s3`: its only S3 implementation.
- `config`: `DeviceLogsProperties`, validated at startup.
- `metrics`: `UploadMetrics`, the only place meters are created.

## Hard rules

Will list:

- Nothing reads the request body before every check has passed. Tomcat sends 100 Continue on the first read, but only
  because `web/ContinueOnReadCustomizer` sets it; its default sends it before any check runs. `ExpectContinueOnTomcatTest`
  fails if either breaks.
- Never return 503. Overload and storage problems are 429.
- Only `trust` reads `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` or `X-Forwarded-For`. Header names come from config.
- Only `storage.s3` imports AWS SDK classes.
- Never log or store the body anywhere but S3. One structured log line per request, without contents.

## When ...

Will hold:

- When adding a rejection: `policy/Rejection.java`, `web/RejectionStatusMapper.java`, `openapi.yaml` and the
  parameterized web test, together.
- When adding a setting: `config/DeviceLogsProperties.java`, `application.yml`, and the Configuration table in the
  design doc.
- When changing a Helm value: say whether it is a repo default or set per environment in GDS.

## Tests

Will say where each kind of test goes (see `src/test/README.md` and `src/test-integration/README.md`), and that unit
tests use the in-memory `LogStorage` fake and a fixed `Clock`, never real S3.

Here are the two commands, both run from the repo root:

- **Whole repository:** `mvn clean verify`
- **Upload service only:** `mvn -pl upload-service -am verify`. The `-am` flag also builds `contract`, which the service depends on.

Both commands also run the LocalStack integration tests (`*IT`) through Failsafe, so Docker has to be running.

Files used:
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `upload-service/CLAUDE.md`
